arxiv-2109-01295.title: Information Symmetry Matters: A Modal-Alternating Propagation Network for Few-Shot Learning
arxiv-2109-01295.creator: Zhong Ji, Zhishen Hou, Xiyao Liu, Yanwei Pang, Jungong Han
arxiv-2109-01295.description: Abstract Semantic information provides intra-class consistency and inter-class discriminability beyond visual concepts, which has been employed in Few-Shot Learning (FSL) to achieve further gains. However, semantic information is only available for labeled samples but absent for unlabeled samples, in which the embeddings are rectified unilaterally by guiding the few labeled samples with semantics.

arxiv-2109-08902.title: Convex Formulation for Planted Quasi-Clique Recovery
arxiv-2109-08902.creator: Sakirudeen A. Abdulsalaam, M. Montaz Ali
arxiv-2109-08902.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the planted quasi-clique or γ \gamma -clique problem. This problem is an extension of the well known planted clique problem which is NP-hard. The maximum quasi-clique problem is applicable in community detection, information retrieval and biology. We propose a convex formulation using nuclear norm minimization for planted quasi-clique recovery.

arxiv-2111-07845.description: Abstract The metric dimension dim ( G ) \dim(G) of a graph G G is the minimum cardinality of a subset S S of vertices of G G such that each vertex of G G is uniquely determined by its distances to S S .

arxiv-2207-03397.title: Asset Trading in Continuous Time: A Cautionary Tale
arxiv-2207-03397.creator: William R. Zame
arxiv-2207-03397.description: Abstract The continuous time model of dynamic asset trading is the central model of modern finance. Because trading cannot in fact take place at every moment of time, it would seem desirable to show that the continuous time model can be viewed as the limit of models in which trading can occur only at (many) discrete moments of time.

arxiv-2305-04287.title: A quantum k-nearest neighbors algorithm based on the Euclidean distance estimation

arxiv-2305-04287.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Enrico Zardini, Enrico Blanzieri, Davide Pastorello. The k k -nearest neighbors ( k k -NN) is a basic machine learning (ML) algorithm, and several quantum versions of it, employing different distance metrics, have been presented in the last few years. Although the Euclidean distance is one of the most widely used distance metrics in ML, it has not received much consideration in the development of these quantum variants.

arxiv-2312-14567.description: Abstract Heavy-ball momentum with decaying learning rates is widely used with SGD for optimizing deep learning models. In Lambek D \textrm{Lambek}^{D} , linear types are used as a syntax for formal grammars, and parsers can be written as linear terms.

pmc-11570907.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Left ventricular free wall rupture (LVFWR) is a rare but serious complication following ST-elevation myocardial infarction (MI), occurring in a small fraction of patients. Left Ventricular Free Wall Rupture presents as three types: There are three types of Left Ventricular Free Wall Rupture: Type 1 with an abrupt tear and high mortality, Type 2 with a slower tear, and Type 3 with aneurysm perforation. Despite reperfusion therapies, LVFWR remains concerning due to increased mortality described from 75% to 90%.

This study aimed to test the Big-5 personality traits as possible predictors of AL in Latinos.

pmc-13005151.title: The more, the better? Stress response in related polyploid ferns
pmc-13005151.creator: Steven Awad, Madeline Kenney, Jennifer Blake-Mahmud
pmc-13005151.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, is common in land plants. Polyploidy causes new gene combinations and is thought to provide an advantage amid the rising temperature and unpredictable precipitation regimes expected under climate change. Using related woodfern species, we investigated the gametophyte physiology of two parent species, Dryopteris intermedia (2n) and Dryopteris expansa (2n) in comparison to their polyploid offspring, Dryopteris campyloptera (4n) . We subjected gametophytes from each species to environmentally stressful heat and drought conditions.
